newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco controller boosts stadium measure.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco controller boosts stadium measure.

text.p: Tax revenues from a planned football stadium and retail complex in San Francisco should cover the city's annual debt service on the bonds proposed for the project, the city controller said.

"In my opinion, if this mall is built and when it is fully operational it should generate new revenues sufficient to pay all, or a substantial portion of, the debt service on these bonds," San Francisco Controller Ed Harrington said in one-page report, released by his office on Thursday.

The proposed stadium and retail project would cost an estimated $537 million, including $250 million to build a stadium for the National Football League's San Francisco 49ers and $200 million for the entertainment and shopping complex.
In February, San Francisco's Board of Supervisors passed a resolution placing up to a $100 million bond measure on the ballot to help build the complex.
If approved by San Francisco voters in June, the ballot proposition would authorize the city to issue lease-revenue bonds in a principal amount not exceeding $100 million.

But because the city's redevelopment agency will be able to issue some bonds based on additional property taxes to be collected from the development, stadium proponents expect the city will only need to issue $80 million of the revenue bonds.
If those bonds are sold for 30 years at 6.0 percent interest, the annual debt service would be an estimated $5.78 million, according to Harrington's report.
A recent poll by the San Francisco Chronicle suggested that the stadium bond would be difficult to pitch to voters.
About 47 percent of the voters surveyed said they opposed the stadium plan while 39 percent said they would support the project. Fourteen percent were still undecided.
